title: Scaling both halves of a mesh split by the same factor never moves the split point
statement: Fix a ratio between two mesh counts as a pair (m_ac, m_cb), and scale BOTH by the same factor Nat.succ k. Then CReal.riemannSum_split_exact's own split-point formula, read at the scaled counts (succ_mul_succ(m_ac,k), succ_mul_succ(m_cb,k)), is CReal.Equiv to the split point computed directly at the base counts (m_ac, m_cb): the two agree exactly, for every k, not merely in the limit. This is gap 1 of CReal.integral_split's remaining assembly (crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/creal/integral.rs's own module documentation, 'the accuracy-parameterized mesh choice'): it makes the refinement factor k free to pick as deep as an accuracy argument needs on all three intervals of a split, without the split point itself drifting as k grows.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.riemannSum_split_scale_invariant : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat) -> CReal.Equiv (CReal.add x0 (CReal.mul (CReal.ofNat (AxNat.succ (AxNat.add (AxNat.add (AxNat.mul x2 x4) x2) x4))) (CReal.mul (CReal.add x1 (CReal.neg x0)) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) (AxNat.add (AxNat.succ (AxNat.add (AxNat.add (AxNat.mul x2 x4) x2) x4)) (AxNat.add (AxNat.add (AxNat.mul x3 x4) x3) x4))))))) (CReal.add x0 (CReal.mul (CReal.ofNat (AxNat.succ x2)) (CReal.mul (CReal.add x1 (CReal.neg x0)) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) (AxNat.add (AxNat.succ x2) x3)))))))))))
